title: What they said at the time

clips.q: It’s not just Pepsi without the color.
People are trained to drink a brown cola, and that’s what they’ll eventually want.
clips.who: **Manager of an Albertson’s supermarket in Dallas**, Los Angeles Times, May 26, 1992[^6]
**Doug Ivester**, Coca-Cola, The New York Times, Dec 15, 1992[^8]

clips.q: They have allowed Pepsi to seize the momentum.
clips.who: **Tom Pirko**, Bevmark, on Coca-Cola, The New York Times, Dec 15, 1992[^8]

clips.q: Everyone is desperate for something innovative. But a lot of this is just appealing to consumers’ perceptions. I don’t think it will last.
clips.who: **Martin J. Friedman**, editor of New Product News, Associated Press, Mar 8, 1993[^14]

clips.q: The Crystal Pepsi products particularly aided first quarter results, but did not significantly impact full year profits.
The future of Crystal is anything but clear.
It would have been nice if I’d made sure the product tasted good.
We’re excited to see this special tour come to life and to celebrate Crystal Pepsi’s last return.
clips.who: **Chad Stubbs**, Pepsi, press release, Jul 19, 2017[^32]. It returned again in 2022.[^34]
